item.title: Windows OpenSSL Not Recognized: Install, Configure PATH and Verify
item.description:
Generating a Facebook key hash failed because Windows did not recognize openssl:

Install a maintained Windows OpenSSL distribution from a trusted source, then add its bin directory to the system Path environment variable—for example:

1

D:\tools\OpenSSL\bin

Open a new terminal and verify:

1

openssl version

item.title: Safely Free Windows Disk Space: Temporary Files, Storage Sense and Cleanup
item.description:
The Windows system drive can gradually lose free space as temporary files, update caches, recycle-bin contents, and application data accumulate.

The original article proposed a batch file that recursively deleted every .tmp, .log, .old, and several other file types across the entire system drive. That approach is too broad: those extensions may contain active application data, diagnostic records, or files required for recovery. A safer process is to use Windows’ built-in cleanup controls.

item.title: Fix Missing DLL Errors on Windows: App Repair, Runtimes and System Files
item.description:
Windows development tools sometimes report that a .dll file is missing. I encountered this while installing Visual Studio 2022:

Avoid downloading individual DLL files from generic DLL sites. A file with the right name may have the wrong version or architecture, may be malicious, and usually does not repair the underlying installation or registration problem.

Use this order instead:

  1. Record the exact DLL name and the application that requested it.

  2. Run the application’s official installer in Repair mode. For Visual Studio, use Visual Studio Installer and repair the selected workloads.

  3. If the DLL belongs to a Microsoft runtime, install or repair the official supported Visual C++ Redistributable for the required x86 or x64 architecture.

  4. Install pending Windows updates and restart.

  5. For suspected Windows component corruption, open an elevated terminal and run:

    1
2

    DISM.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
sfc /scannow

  6. Check Windows Security quarantine history and the application’s event or installer logs.

item.title: Create a Windows Wi-Fi Hotspot: Internet Sharing and Troubleshooting
item.description:
A Windows laptop or desktop with a supported wireless adapter can share an Ethernet, Wi-Fi, or cellular Internet connection without third-party hotspot software.

Use the built-in settings

On current Windows releases:

  1. Open Settings → Network & internet → Mobile hotspot.
  2. Choose the Internet connection to share.
  3. Select Wi-Fi as the sharing method when available.
  4. Edit the network name and use a strong, unique password.
  5. Turn on Mobile hotspot, then connect the other device using those credentials.

The exact labels can vary by Windows release and hardware. Older netsh wlan set hostednetwork instructions depend on a legacy hosted-network driver and are no longer supported by many modern adapters, so the Settings interface is the preferred method.
